newsitem.title: USA: House passes intelligence spending bill.
newsitem.headline: House passes intelligence spending bill.

text.p: The House approved by voice vote Wednesday a spending bill for intelligence activities at 12 federal agencies.
The bill covered intelligence activities at a dozen federal agencies, including the Central Intelligence Agency, the National Security Agency and the Federal Bureau of Investigation.
Most of the intelligence authorisation bill was secret, but it was believed to be about $30 billion for fiscal 1998.
A similar, but not identical, bill was pending in the Senate.

Although the spending levels are not made public, Intelligence Committee Chairman Porter Goss, a Florida Republican, said it is 0.7 percent more than President Clinton asked for in his budget. Republicans defeated Democratic amendments that would have rolled spending back.
The bill placed emphasis not just on collecting intelligence but on analysing and disseminating it.
It also placed the office of the CIA director back within the CIA -- replacing language that was taken out by accident in this year's intelligence authorisation bill.
